meaning:
ἄφρων, -ον genitive -ονος
(φρήν), [in LXX for כְּסִיל, נָבָל, etc. ;]
without reason, senseless, foolish, expressing "want of mental sanity and sobriety, a reckless and inconsiderate habit of mind" (Hort; cf. MM, see word): Luk.11:40 12:20, Rom.2:20, 1Co.15:36, 2Co.11:16 12:6 12:11, 1Pe.2:15; opposite to φρόνιμος, 2Co.11:19; to συνιέντες, Eph.2:17.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?
a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babies, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth.
You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.
I say again, let no one think me foolish. But if so, yet receive me as foolish, that I also may boast a little.
Therefore don’t be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
For this is the will of God, that by well-doing you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish men:
